prompt.es: Escribe el mensaje de aclaración: afirmaciones, fuentes, dudas y consejo final.

answer.text: Hello everyone. A viral post claims that the city is closing the public pool forever, but that is misleading. According to the council's statement, the pool will close for six weeks for repairs, starting on 1 June, and it will open again in July. The post also says that five thousand people signed a petition; however, the local newspaper reported that only about five hundred people have signed it. A spokesperson denied any plan to sell the pool, and nobody has confirmed that it will close for good. The word forever exaggerates the news, so this looks like a rumour. Before you share a post like this, please verify it with two reliable sources. Thank you!
accepted: Hello everyone. A viral post claims that the city is closing the public pool forever, but that is misleading. The post also says that five thousand people signed a petition; however, the local newspaper reported that only about five hundred people have signed it. A spokesperson denied any plan to sell the pool, and nobody has confirmed that it will close for good. The word forever exaggerates the news, so this looks like a rumour. Before you share a post like this, please verify it with two reliable sources. Thank you!

Please read before you share. A viral post says that the public pool will close forever, but the council's statement says it will only close for six weeks for repairs from 1 June. The post also claims that five thousand people signed a petition, but according to the local newspaper, only about five hundred did. A spokesperson denied selling the pool, and a closure for good is still unconfirmed. So the post is a hoax or, at least, a story that exaggerates. Always check two reliable sources before sharing a post like this, and remember that a screenshot is not proof.

Correction: a viral post claims that the pool will close forever. According to the council, the pool will close for repairs for six weeks, and it will open again in July. The newspaper reported that the petition has about five hundred signatures, not five thousand. A spokesperson denied planning to sell the pool, and nobody has confirmed that it will close for good. The word forever exaggerates the story, and the post gives no context. Before sharing it, please verify it with two sources, because a rumour can travel faster than the facts.
